title: Large credit-repair redress dispatch can widen reach without proving usable recovery
source_unit: Federal Trade Commission FES credit-repair pyramid-scheme refund distribution
geography: United States consumers harmed by Financial Education Services and related credit-repair operations

denominator.unit: affected customers sent FTC checks; aggregate recipient count

distribution_amount.unit: more than U.S. dollars in checks sent to affected customers

underlying_harm.value: FTC alleged that the operation promised easy credit repair while charging consumers and recruiting participants into a pyramid scheme

payment_channel.value: Mailed checks administered through Analytics Consulting LLC

acceptance_window.value: Recipients were instructed to cash checks within 90 days

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official FTC refund-distribution press release; harm allegation, distribution, payment channel, and acceptance window are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The public release does not disclose delivery success, check cashing, returned checks, reissue, individual amounts, credit-score or debt correction, residual loss, repeat exposure, trust, switching, or household recovery.
observations.subgroup: Consumers affected by the FES credit-repair operation who were included in the FTC distribution; no complete historical-harm denominator.
observations.counterinterpretation: A large dispatch can expand formal reach while usable receipt remains conditioned on address, attention, banking access, and the short cashing window; the distribution is not a prevalence or recovery estimate.

related_sources.claim: The FTC refund page identifies Analytics Consulting as administrator, repeats the aggregate check distribution and 90-day cashing instruction, and supplies a recipient phone route; it does not publish cashed, returned, reissued, or recovery totals.
The FTC case record supplies the enforcement context for the FES refund route.

boundary: This record establishes a named credit-repair harm allegation and a large FTC check distribution with an explicit cashing window. It does not establish individual receipt, adequate restoration of credit or money, later household security, trust, switching, or exit.
